title: Factors affecting courts as law-makers

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches how precedent, judicial conservatism or activism, cost and time, and standing limit courts as law-makers; one covers NGOs and environmental enforcement and the other covers the Children's Court and rehabilitation.

draft.title: Factors affecting courts as law-makers
card: Standing
a person must be directly affected by a legal issue to bring a case. Courts cannot start changing the law on their own, so they wait for suitable cases.
Cost and time
court cases can be expensive and slow. This can stop people bringing cases, so some issues never reach a court.
Precedent
lower courts must follow binding precedent from higher courts in their hierarchy. This makes the law stable but limits how far a judge can change it.
Conservatism or activism
a conservative judge keeps to existing law and leaves reform to parliament. An activist judge is more willing to develop the law to meet new social needs.
draft.remember: Courts can only make law when a suitable case reaches them, and precedent and judicial approach shape what they do with it.

a.q: Why can a court not change an unfair law as soon as a judge notices it?
opts: It must wait for a case from someone with standing
It may only change laws that parliament has just passed
It can only change the law after a public vote
It needs the approval of the Attorney-General first
a.why: Courts make law only when a dispute is brought by a person with standing. Judges cannot start reform on their own. The idea that they must wait for parliament is tempting, but courts can develop common law without a new Act.
a.clue: Who has to start a court case?

b.q: Two judges hear similar cases. Judge Ng follows earlier decisions closely and says reform is for parliament. Judge Roy develops the law to meet new social needs. How would you describe them?
opts: Ng is conservative and Roy is activist
Ng is activist and Roy is conservative
Both are conservative, as both are bound by precedent
Both are activist, as both are making law in court
b.why: A conservative judge sticks to existing law and leaves change to parliament. An activist judge is more willing to develop the law. Precedent binds both judges, so it does not show who is conservative or activist.
b.clue: Which judge leaves reform to parliament?

a.best: It must wait for a case from someone with standing

b.best: Ng is conservative and Roy is activist
